On that note, if you haven't taken the airpoppedpill yet, get on it. Microwave popcorn is full of nitrates and other nasty shit, plus you always overpay per serving, no matter how cheap the price. Don't bother with the stove stuff either, it's not the easiest way.

If you don't know how, here's the rundown:

  • Get you a bag of popping kernels for about $1-2. One teaspoon is one serving, so your bag will last a long time.
  • Get you some paper bags. Put kernels into a bag, roll down the top tightly, but leave room in the bag for the kernels to pop.
  • Microwave the bag and contents on high for ~3 minutes. For my particular microwave, 3:10 is the perfect length of time for maximum crisp. If you do it right, you should eventually get it to where you only have one or two unpopped kernels, unlike what you'd get with prepackaged shite.
  • If you want, flavor your popcorn. I like to toss mine with either extra virgin olive oil or coconut oil to start. Don't bother with buying popcorn oil or sprays, they're a ripoff; overpriced, barely flavored canola oil usually. Just use regular canola oil if that's what you want.
  • After the oil, I use Kernel Seasons to add flavor. My favorite ones are Ranch, White Cheddar, Sour Cream & Onion, and Garlic Parmesan. I keep at least one of each on hand so I can mix and match as I like.

If you really like homemade popcorn (because it's one of the healthiest snacks you can enjoy anytime IMO), get you one of these purpose-made silicone air poppers. I recently got one and it works great -- dishwasher safe, plus I don't go through paper bags like crazy anymore.

If you do get one of these poppers, it might come with instructions telling you to add oil and seasoning directly in before popping. I don't recommend this because the popper is harder to clean afterward, and you lose control over distribution. Oil and season after you pop so you have full control.
